title: Coherence of an epimorphic quotient with quasi-compact kernel pair
statement: Let $\mathcal E$ be a coherent Grothendieck topos [def-trf-coherent-topos] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:P\to A$ be an epimorphism in $\mathcal E$, with $P$ coherent. If its kernel-pair object $R=P\times_A P$ is quasi-compact, then $A$ is coherent. Here the two projections $R\rightrightarrows P$ are the pullback of $p$ with itself; epimorphism means right cancellation against every object of $\mathcal E$, and quasi-compact and coherent have exactly the meanings in [def-trf-coherent-topos].

Context: literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Exposé XI, proof of Lemma 2.5, printed p. 179; complete proposed argument in report.md.

proof.text: By [def-trf-coherent-topos], the coherent object $P$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply the epimorphic-image clause of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus] to the given epimorphism $p:P\to A$. Thus $A$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Agent assembly using lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus: Agent auxiliary extracting returned proof steps 1–2 of lem-trf-coherent-epimorphic-quotient. Tag 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), Tag 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), Tag 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact). Local lifting and universal jointly epimorphic families are the sheaf-theoretic expansion; the empty coproduct case is included explicitly.

proof.text: Fix the small full generating subcategory $\mathcal G$ of coherent objects from [def-trf-coherent-topos]. To establish the condition of the lifted-generator test, let $K,L\in\mathcal G$ and $k:K\to P$, $l:L\to P$ be arbitrary. Coherence of $K,L$ gives their quasi-compactness. Coherence of $P$ gives its quasi-separatedness, and $R=P\times_A P$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-kernel-pair-restriction-quasicompact] with this same morphism $p$ and these maps $k,l$. Its conclusion says that $K\times_{pk,A,pl}L$ is quasi-compact. Thus the generator condition holds for all pairs of objects and maps, with precisely the composites $pk,pl$ as structure maps to $A$.

source.place: Agent assembly using lem-trf-kernel-pair-restriction-quasicompact: Agent auxiliary extracting returned proof step 6 of lem-trf-coherent-epimorphic-quotient: kernel-pair restriction as two fibre products over P and two applications of quasi-separatedness. Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) supplies the sectionwise limits for the explicit natural isomorphism; quasi-compactness uses the definition of quasi-separated objects, not a coherence-of-products theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-lifted-generator-quasiseparated-test], clause (2), to $\mathcal G$ and the epimorphism $p$. The condition proved in step 2 implies that $A$ is quasi-separated. Together with its quasi-compactness from step 1 this is coherence by [def-trf-coherent-topos]. The finite-cover calculus and the generator test include empty families, so no nonemptiness assumption is introduced.
